properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 8:28PM MDT until September 15 at 9:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Grand County in east central Utah...

* Until 930 PM MDT.

* At 828 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of West Central Grand County, and portions of
I-70 between mile marker 175 and mile marker 190.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 15 at 11:10PM EDT until September 15 at 11:45PM EDT by NWS Detroit/Pontiac MI
properties.description:
At 1110 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Adrian, moving
east at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe storm will be near...
Blissfield around 1115 PM EDT.
Deerfield around 1120 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this severe thunderstorm include Jasper,
Weston, Ogden Center, Riga, Palmyra, Fairfield, Sand Creek, and
Holloway.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 15 at 4:11PM CDT until September 17 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

East Nishnabotna River At Red Oak affecting Montgomery County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...East Nishnabotna River at Red Oak.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Lowland flooding begins along the west
bank.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 19.7 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will then fall below flood stage by late tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.6
feet on 06/15/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 15 at 8:10PM CDT until September 16 at 3:30PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Adair County in southwestern Iowa...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 807 PM CDT, Emergency management reported numerous closed
roads in the warned area, with water nearing Highway 25 south of
Greenfield. Flooding is already occurring. Between 2 and 4 inches
of rain have fallen.
- An additional 1 inch or more is possible in the warned area
through the overnight hours. Impacted streams include the Middle
River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Greenfield, Stuart, Adair, Fontanelle, Orient, Bridgewater,
Greenfield Municipal Airport and Nodaway Park.
- This includes Interstate 80 between mile markers 73 and 96.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

weather.gov/desmoines/water.

properties.description:

radar estimated 1.5 and 3 inches of rain fell earlier this evening.
Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams and
normally dry washes.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
West Poker Mountain, Black River.
properties.instruction:

muddy and impassable.
